messages:
olivia: Ran a perf run on AWQ load tests and hit a repeatable OOM during canary. Not a single large allocation — lots of small frees and a growing fragmented kv cache :eyes:

olivia: Repro command: `curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood/v1/gen -d '{"model":"awq-gptq-13b","prompt":"<long chat>","max_tokens":1024}'`

maria: Paste of pprof heap snapshot from CUDA host profiler attached in-line:
```
pprof gpu_heap:
  total: 1.45GB
  kv_cache: 720MB (many small extents)
  mini_pool_freelist: 260MB
  workspace: 340MB
  other: 130MB
```

maria: Looks like fragmentation in the mini-pool allocator + kv cache dtype mismatch. Kernel-selection-v2 changed fallback allocs to buddy and increased external fragmentation.

tariq: I saw the same pattern in nightly on dedicated; fragmentation grows with many short-lived batched requests (batch size 1-4). Batching heuristics are making tiny workspaces that thrash the freelist.

ryan: What if we implement mini-pool reclamation: periodically attempt to coalesce adjacent free mini-slices back to the slabpool or compact into a secondary free list? Cheap GC every N allocations.

olivia: Proposed patch: reclaim on allocation path when freelist_count > THRESH and failed_allocs > N. Quick pseudo: `if (freelist_frag > 0.25 && failed_allocs>3) reclaim()`

zhao: Also we should sanity-check KV cache dtype. AWQ stores per-kv in approx int8/packed formats, but our runtime still reserves fp32-equivalent workspace for some fallback kernels. If we force kv dtype=float16 for serving path we drop ~40% memory. But need to ensure kernel supports fp16 matmul gather.

maria: Right — observed mixed-precision pitfall: FP8 config paired with FP16 KV causes small numeric diffs but generally fine for retrieval; FP8->FP16 conversion during decode spikes temporary workspace. That transient buffer is what triggers OOM.

tariq: Short term mitigation: change batcher to prefer splitting a large request into two sequential runs when workspace + kv > threshold. i.e., dynamic_batch_split= true for low-memory devices.

ryan: I added quick profiler numbers after toggling mini-pool reclamation branch (notes):
```
before: peak_gpu=1460MB
after:  peak_gpu=1188MB (-272MB)
kv_peak: before 720MB -> after 480MB
num_reclaims: 203 per 10k requests
p99_latency: +6ms
```

zhao: +6ms p99 is acceptable vs OOM. We should gate this behind env flags: `RW_MINI_POOL_RECLAIM=1` and `RW_DYNAMIC_BATCH_SPLIT=1`.

olivia: Agreed. Also add a KV dtype opt `rw_kv_dtype=fp16|fp32|auto` default auto -> prefers fp16 if kernel supports it. Need a sanity check in model-compatibility table.

maria: Edge case: GPTQ quantized models sometimes return slightly different tokenization/softmax scaling; add regression test in evallist for a handful of prompts when enabling fp16 kv. If regression > threshold, fall back to fp32.

tooling-bot: deploy-plan created -> canary: eng-runtime staging -> 50% nodes with reclaim + kv_fp16 -> monitor OOMs 1h, p95 latency, and generation perplexity.

tariq: I'll prototype reclamation algorithm tonight and push draft PR. Will also add counters for reclaimed_bytes and reclaim_calls.

olivia: Thanks. If we can get the kv dtype toggle and reclamation in canary this week we can probably close the regression. :thumbsup:

ryan: One more note — resize workspace ceiling helps: `export RW_WS_MAX=400M` reduced workspace transient from 340MB -> 220MB which compounds savings. Combine all three mitigations for best effect.

zhao: Putting checklist in PR: 1) mini-pool reclaim implementation + metrics; 2) dynamic batch split; 3) kv_dtype opt and model compatibility matrix; 4) evallist regressions; 5) canary plan.

olivia: Perfect. Tagging @sre to watch alerts when canary rolls out.

sre: watching and will mute noisy alerts, escalate if OOM rate > 0.5%
